item.text:
**8B.7 Research Note: Félix Tshisekedi, 2024**
Overall reading: **mixed, with limited positive movement on ceasefire/diplomacy and macro-stabilization, but no broad countrywide improvement in security, rights, or living conditions.** The positive signals are mostly **partial, late, and fragile**; the negative signals are broader and more persistent.

| Claim-level item | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Short claim-level summary | Q IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Temporary de-escalation in the east, but not a durable peace dividend | UN Office at Geneva | 2024-09-30 | https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/news/2024/09/98156/collective-effort-essential-get-dr-congo-firm-path-to-peace | UN reported a notable reduction in fighting after the 30 July ceasefire and an active DRC-Rwanda dialogue framework. This is the best evidence that Tshisekedi’s peace-oriented diplomacy produced some directional movement, but the same report says peace was not yet won, and late-December reporting shows the Angola summit collapsed, so the gain was fragile and incomplete. | `8B.7` |
| Security outcomes stayed weak despite harsher discipline and military mobilization | Reuters / Straits Times | 2024-07-04 | https://www.straitstimes.com/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say | Reuters reported army disarray, weak logistics, demoralized troops, and heavy reliance on poorly controlled Wazalendo proxies; Tshisekedi had instructed that the militias be brought in line, but the force remained fragmented. This cuts against a clean “things moved in the intended direction” reading for security governance. | `8B.7` |
| Macro-stability moved somewhat in the claimed direction, but only partially | IMF | 2024-07-03 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr | IMF said the authorities maintained prudent macro policies, avoided monetary financing, improved revenue mobilization, and strengthened reserves, while inflation eased. This supports a limited stabilization success story, but the same IMF assessment says the security crisis in the east, fiscal slippage, and slow reform execution kept the improvement modest. | `8B.7` |
| Living conditions and human-rights indicators did not move much in the claimed direction | Amnesty International / Human Rights Watch / World Bank | 2024-06-24 to 2024-04-03 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/ | Amnesty said Tshisekedi had made little to no progress on prior human-rights pledges, with shrinking civic space, underfunded services, and worsening conflict. HRW likewise said 2024 saw continued repression and little systemic reform. The World Bank added that growth would not translate into better living conditions without much more ambitious reform, which is strong counterevidence to any broad directional improvement claim. | `8B.7` |
| Some technocratic and oversight steps were real, but they were narrow and offset by patronage pressures | Reuters / DRC presidency / Court of Accounts / World Bank | 2024-04-01 to 2024-10-07 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/ | The appointment of Judith Suminwa and later of a finance technocrat, plus support for Court of Accounts oversight, show real movement toward competence and anti-corruption guardrails. But opaque procurement reporting, cabinet bargaining delays, and broader governance criticism mean these gains were limited rather than transformative. | `8B.7` |
| Democratic restraint moved in the opposite direction on the term-limit question | Reuters | 2024-10-24 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-over-constitutional-reform-plans-2024-10-24/ | Reuters reported Tshisekedi created a commission to explore constitutional revisions that could remove term limits and enable a third term. If the relevant revealed aim is preserving open contestability and constitutional rotation, this is negative evidence; if the revealed aim is regime survival, it points the other way. Either way, it does not support a clean pro-democratic outcome trend. | `8B.7` |

**Best synthesis for 8B.7**
- **Yes, partly** for ceasefire/diplomatic de-escalation and macro stabilization.
- **No, overall** for broad security, human-rights, and living-conditions outcomes.
- The strongest positive evidence is **temporary and sector-specific**.
- The strongest negative evidence is **structural and repeated**.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single independent source that cleanly quantifies year-over-year improvement across the whole set of outcome indicators Tshisekedi claimed to want.
- The evidence base is therefore **mixed narrative evidence**, not a clean before/after statistical panel.
- The most defensible inference is that 2024 delivered **partial tactical movement** in peace and stabilization, but **not durable broad outcome improvement** once inherited conflict and external constraints are accounted for.
